subject.title: [Feature]: Fallback approval mode + model attribution in messages

question: Should OpenClaw add a core opt-in approval gate before executing configured model fallbacks, and if so what config scope, timeout behavior, and delivery surface should own it?
rationale: The remaining request changes fallback runtime behavior and adds operator-facing config; OpenClaw policy treats fallback behavior and config surface as compatibility- and product-sensitive.

options.title: Design A Core Default-Off Gate
options.body: Define a per-agent or per-session approval contract with timeout behavior, denial semantics, same-channel delivery, and upgrade-safe config before implementation.

options.title: Keep Fallback Automatic
options.body: Treat response-prefix attribution, fallback notices, strict user-selected models, and explicit empty fallback lists as the supported control model and close this direction as not planned.

options.title: Route Through Extension Design First
options.body: Define a plugin or approval-event hook for fallback decisions before adding a one-off core model config key.

recommendation.title: Design A Core Default-Off Gate
recommendation.body: Define a per-agent or per-session approval contract with timeout behavior, denial semantics, same-channel delivery, and upgrade-safe config before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history on prefix context, per-agent fallback config, and core/plugin product boundaries for this decision.
